title: Cooling and Environmental Monitoring
summary: Use synthetic temperature, airflow, humidity, and fan-status trends to investigate a cooling alert.
objectives: Interpret a synthetic environmental trend and identify relevant evidence.
Explain why a rising temperature requires investigation and safe escalation.

vocab.def: The direction of temperature values over time.
The amount of water vapor in air.
The point where air enters equipment or a space.

sections.heading: Environment affects reliability
sections.body: Equipment produces heat, and operations teams monitor temperature, airflow, cooling status, and sometimes humidity. Trends can reveal that a condition is changing.

sections.heading: Investigate a rising rack temperature
sections.body: A synthetic scenario may include a temperature trend, fan status, blocked-airflow clue, and cooling alarm. Compare all clues before deciding what to report.

sections.heading: Do not service equipment
sections.body: Students may analyze diagrams and data. HVAC service, equipment opening, and industrial cooling work require qualified supervision and remain outside this course.

practice.prompt: A simulated rack temperature rises while fan status changes to warning. Write the evidence, a safe next step, and the escalation point.

quiz.question: What does a temperature trend help an operator understand?
options: Whether a condition is changing over time
The exact root cause by itself
quiz.answer: Whether a condition is changing over time

lab.objective: Investigate a synthetic cooling alert using a trend table and environmental status clues.

reflectionPrompt: Why is a trend more useful than one temperature reading alone?
